Reduce Replicates to Mean and Standard Error

Source: R/statistics.R
reduceReplicates.Rd

Replaces the replicates of each condition by their mean and the standard error of the mean.

Usage

reduceReplicates(
  data,
  select = "condition",
  datatrans = NULL,
  keep = NULL,
  weighted = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
reduceReplicates(
  data,
  select = "condition",
  datatrans = NULL,
  keep = NULL,
  weighted = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the columns name (observable), time, value and condition, plus any further columns that define conditions.

select

Names of the columns whose values, together with name, time and condition, define a condition. Default "condition".

datatrans

Character, an expression in x applied to value before the reduction, for example "log(x)". Default NULL.

keep

Names of columns that are kept although their values differ within a condition; the first value is used. Default NULL.

weighted

Logical. If TRUE, mean and standard error are weighted by 1 / sigma^2 from the column sigma of data. Default FALSE.

Value

A data frame with the columns

time

Time of the measurement.

value

Mean of the replicates.

sigma

Standard error of the mean, NA for a single measurement.

n

Number of replicates.

name

Observable.

condition

The values of the select columns other than name and time, joined by "_".

followed by the kept columns.

Details

A column not in select is kept when it has the same value for all replicates of every condition, otherwise it is dropped with a message.

See also

fitErrorModel()

Examples

data <- data.frame(name = "y", time = rep(c(0, 1, 2), each = 3),
                   value = c(1.0, 1.2, 0.9, 0.6, 0.5, 0.7, 0.3, 0.2, 0.25),
                   condition = "ctrl", replicate = rep(1:3, 3))
reduceReplicates(data)
#> Dropped columns: replicate
#>   time    value      sigma n name condition
#> 1    0 1.033333 0.08819171 3    y      ctrl
#> 4    1 0.600000 0.05773503 3    y      ctrl
#> 7    2 0.250000 0.02886751 3    y      ctrl
